subject: Problem formulating a marked point process model

messages.author: aae8e9f66c6ae74f
messages.subject: Problem formulating a marked point process model
parts:
Hi, 

I'm trying to create a sort of marked point process model and am not quite getting the format right (I think - whenever I try running it I get endless messages 

"Function: GMRFLib_build_sparse_matrix_TAUCS(), Line: 758, Thread: 0
Variable evaluates to NAN or INF. idx=(1577,1577). I will try to fix it..."
).

I suspect I'm getting something wrong in the structure, and it might be to do with the Intercept (I've played around a lot to see if I can isolate things), but I can't quite work out how this relates to the int.vp (an intercept for the points object only - does that makes sense?).

Essentially I have two data stacks, one of point data, one of background data, which I combine and then fit with a log link and appropriate (I think!) spde model.

Each point belongs to one of two groups (indicated by a 0 / 1 column called selous in the points data) and I have a few spatial covariates. A key question is whether there is a strong impact of the mark on the relationship with the covariates. I have tried to test this by specifying an interaction between the mark and the covariates in the formula, but this could be completely wrong! 

My code is:

library(INLA)
load("testData.Rdata")

# stk.ip - defines the background data
# stk.points - defines the point data
# mesh - mesh for...
# spde - the spatial structure

# important note: selous only appears in the points data, because it is a property of the points (a mark)
# other data should be present for both points and background

form <- formula(resp ~ 0 + selous * (PA2 + PA3 + PA4 + rivers.s) + int.vp + Intercept +
                  f(i, model = spde))

# combine data stacks:
stck <- inla.stack(stk.ip, stk.points)

#priors:
cont.fix <- list(
  mean = list(int.vp = 0),
  mean.intercept = 0,
  prec = list(int.vp = 1),
  prec.intercept = 0.001
)


# Fit model
mod <- inla(form, family = "poisson", control.family = list(list(link = "log")), 
            data = inla.stack.data(stck), 
            verbose = TRUE, 
            control.results = list(return.marginals.random = FALSE, 
                                   return.marginals.predictor = FALSE), 
            control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(stck),  link = NULL, compute = TRUE), 
            control.fixed = cont.fix,                                                                                                    
            Ntrials = inla.stack.data(stck)$Ntrials,
            E = inla.stack.data(stck)$e, 
            num.threads = 6)


And the testData.Rdata file can be found here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Spf_uJFyKvf_EXyPh5h0P0wHp85wTdJs/view?usp=sharing 

Any ideas could be most welcome! It's probably something fairly basic - I'm still not getting my head around all of this.

Thanks!

Colin

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Problem formulating a marked point process model
parts:
this means that some likelihood contribution have been detected as NAN
or INF. this usually comes from the optimizer diverging, which again can
happen if the model is to vague and/or the data not that informative.

yes, there is something going on

first the 'e' variable is (when non-zero) pretty big, like ~ 1E8,you may
want to scale the problem/data so its more 'well behaved

it seems like all 'resp' is 0 when e > 0 and 1 when e=0. I guess this is
not what you want ?

Thanks!

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Problem formulating a marked point process model
parts:
The e>0,resp=1, e=0,resp=1 thing is how the lgcp likelihood is implemented, so that's by INLA design...

But the scaling is a likely problem, yes. If your space is in metres (default UTM coordinates, for example), then rescaling to kilometres is highly recommended.
This would change the scale of E by a factor 1e6, so 1e8 would become a much more well-behaved 100.

Finn

On Fri, 31 Jul 2020 at 15:58, Finn Lindgren <finn.l...@gmail.com> wrote:

The e>0,resp=1, e=0,resp=1 thing is how the lgcp likelihood is implemented, so that's by INLA design...

But the scaling is a likely problem, yes. If your space is in metres (default UTM coordinates, for example), then rescaling to kilometres is highly recommended.
This would change the scale of E by a factor 1e6, so 1e8 would become a much more well-behaved 100.

Finn
